correctness.rationale: Both rates are strictly positive and bounded above; uniformly over initial states, in a fixed block there is positive probability of absorption before a reset, or of a reset followed by absorption during a reset-free interval. A uniform positive block bound follows by dominating resets by the upper rate and retaining the lower-rate clock; it gives finite uniformly bounded means. Independently, kill the environment at reset with subgenerator Q−Λ and couple it to Brownian absorption before the first reset. Writing B_0=Λ−Q, the expected pre-event occupation operator is K=∫Pr(τ_B>t)exp(−tB_0)dt=B_0^(−1)(I−exp(−ℓ√B_0)). The renewal load is K1 and its phase-preserving continuation kernel is KΛ. Rearrangement gives (I−h(B_0)Q)v=h(B_0)1; the normalized symmetric/antisymmetric basis yields the stated Schur complement with a positive denominator. For ν→∞, the fast eigenmode inverse 1/h_+ is superalgebraically small also after one r derivative on compact sets. Dividing by νh_+ leaves h_-/p up to O(ν⁻³) in C¹; λ_-=r−η²/ν+O(ν⁻³) and p=1−η²/ν²+O(ν⁻⁴) yield both coefficients and uniformity. The slow limit is the two-rate average; strict convexity follows since the derivative with respect to z of the numerator of 4r³h″ is e^z(z²−3z+3)>0. The derivative of h crosses zero uniquely at the positive z_*; Taylor expansion with c bounded proves the stated offset and the signed comparison, excluding balanced c. The difference derivative is strictly negative in a fixed neighborhood for large ν, and bracketing c on either side of ccrit puts the unique zero at r_*+ccrit/ν+O(ν⁻²). A fresh physical-coordinate renewal solve reproduced ccrit≈22.2301179837920 for ℓ=η=1 and scaled shifts 22.46642, 22.25350, 22.23245 at ν=10³,10⁴,10⁵, respectively. Those computations are corroboration, not the uniform-limit proof.
residual_risks: Only a local zero near r_* at rapid switching; no conclusion at the exactly balanced coordinate to this order. No claims for a zero intensity or reset of the environment.

value.rationale: The usual first-order fast-refresh calculation cannot decide the sign at the Poisson optimum. The positive second-order effect and rate shift sharply separate improvement from deterioration at the same mean rate, and quantify the correction where this ambiguity matters.
